name: Updated MiniBooNE Neutrino Oscillation Results with Increased Data and New Background Studies
notes: The collaboration's own wording is 'excess', never 'discovery' or 'observation'; result_type is 'anomaly' accordingly.

An earlier report (Phys. Rev. Lett. 121, 221801 (2018), arXiv:1805.12028, src:miniboone-prl-2018-excess) found a 4.5σ charged-current quasielastic-only excess of 381.2±85.2 events with a smaller exposure; this record uses the 2021 combined/updated figure as the primary claim and cites the 2018 paper as a supporting source.

The 2021 abstract also reports a combined LSND+MiniBooNE significance of 6.0σ, not recorded as this entity's own significance since it is a joint result with a different experiment (LSND, not in this atlas wave).

significance.quote: A total excess of 638.0 ± 132.8 electron-like events (4.8σ)

summary.plain: MiniBooNE saw more low-energy, electron-like flashes of light in its detector than it expected from known physics: 638 more than predicted, a 4.8-out-of-a-possible-many-sigma excess. No one has agreed on why.
summary.technical: Combined neutrino- and antineutrino-mode MiniBooNE data (24.11e20 POT total) show a 4.8sigma excess of 638.0+-132.8 low-energy electron-like events over the background-only prediction, updating the original 2018 result. The origin of the excess (sterile neutrinos, a misestimated background, or new physics) remains unresolved; MicroBooNE's 2021 search (result:microboone-no-low-energy-excess-2021) found no corresponding excess in its own single-final-state analyses.

title: Updated MiniBooNE Neutrino Oscillation Results with Increased Data and New Background Studies
why_it_matters: If it is not an underestimated background, the MiniBooNE excess would require physics beyond the three-neutrino Standard Model, such as a sterile neutrino or new interactions; it motivated the entire Fermilab Short-Baseline Neutrino programme (MicroBooNE, SBND, ICARUS) built to pin down its cause.
